text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London deepened their losses by the close on Friday afternoon, after being pressured by a weaker raws market in New York. Front month May ended $2.30 lower at $310.90 per tonne, just 20 cents off the low, ahead of the contract's expiry next week. Less demand for EU sugars should limit physical delivery against May whites and the chance of a squeeze on short positions, traders said. August closed $1.70 softer at $310.00 per tonne, also near its low.

Raw sugar futures in New York settled weaker but above lows as steady buying in the May/July spread limited losses, dealers said. The recent move to seven-month highs prompted early speculative selling, which pressured spot May to the low of 11.23 cents amid a lack of buying. Steady short covering and refiner buying in the May/July spread emerged by mid-morning and lifted prices off the lows to end only slightly weaker. May finished off 0.04 cent at 11.33 cents/lb after trading from 11.34 and 11.23 cents. The back months settled 0.01 lower to up 0.02.

UNITED STATES - Production in 1996/97 continues to be sluggish. Total output in January 1997 reached 913,916 short tons, raw value, down from last year's 942,000 tons. This brought cumulative production in the first four months of 1996/97 (October/January) up to 4.788 mn tons against 4.919 mn tons in 1995/96. Total output in 1995/96 amounted to 7.358 mn tons compared to 7.891 mn tons in 1994/95. The total for 1996/97 is expected to reach 7.215 mn tons, according to the USDA's April projection. This is somewhat down on the 7.235 mn tons expected in March.

Besides the projection for output, the USDA changed its forecast for domestic deliveries, which now stands at 9.750 mn tons, slightly down on the March figure of 9.800 mn tons. The changes resulted in a stocks to use ratio of 14.4 per cent for April, up from 14.0 per cent in March. In May, the USDA will decide whether to increase the tariff rate import quota by another 220,000 tons. If the stocks to use ratio is 15.5 per cent or less on the review date, the quota automatically goes up 220,000 tons. If it is higher the tranche is cancelled. As most of the figures for 1996/97 are based on a rather firm statistical basis at this time of the year, it is unlikely that the May quota increase will be cancelled.

SPAIN - Sugar imports in December 1996 amounted to 25,290 tonnes, up from last year's 21,745 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first half of 1996/97 (July/December) up to 195,526 tonnes compared to 159,803 tonnes in July/December 1995. Total imports in 1995/96 (July/June) reached 353,193 tonnes against 257,273 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in July/December 1996 were France with 114,434 tonnes whites against 92,868 tonnes, Germany with 29,599 tonnes compared to 26,333 tonnes and Belgium-Luxembourg with 15,267 tonnes, up from 6,774 tonnes. Sugar exports in December 1996 amounted to 12,654 tonnes, down from 22,174 tonnes exported in December 1995. This brought cumulative exports in July/December 1996 up to 119,870 tonnes, down from 127,555 tonnes in the same year ago period. Total exports in 1995/96 amounted to 208,130 tonnes against 195,960 tonnes in 1994/95. FINLAND - Sugar exports in December 1996 amounted to 2,685 tonnes, raw value, which brought cumulative exports in the first quarter of 1996/97 (October/December) up to 15,910 tonnes compared to 17,246 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 49,721 tonnes compared to 6,763 tonnes in 1994/95. The major country of destination in October/December 1996 was Estonia with 6,124 tonnes whites against 4,943 tonnes. Cumulative sugar imports in October/December 1996 amounted to 9,948 tonnes, up from 1,000 tonnes in October/December 1995. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 48,087 tonnes against 52,647 tonnes in 1994/95. The major country of origin in October/December 1996 was Fiji with 9,878 tonnes raws against nil.

The state-run Trading Corporation of Pakistan (TCP) recently said it had invited tenders for the import of 50,000 tonnes of crystal white refined sugar to reach Karachi by June and July. A TCP official, who asked not to be named, said the TCP had asked suppliers for shipment of 25,000 tonnes of sugar to reach Karachi not later than June 20, 1997 and the remaining 25,000 tonnes by July 10, 1997. Tenders will be opened on May 3, 1997, in the presence of bidders or their representatives, it was added.
